newsitem.title: JAPAN: SANYO SEC SAYS NINE INSURERS AGREE TO LOAN DELAY.
newsitem.headline: SANYO SEC SAYS NINE INSURERS AGREE TO LOAN DELAY.

text.p: Sanyo Securities Co Ltd said on Friday that nine life insurers had agreed to a three-month delay on repayment of its subordinated loans.
A spokesman for Sanyo Securities could not immediately provide the conditions which allowed for the delay.
On Thursday, Nippon Life Insurance Co, one of the nine insurers, said it had agreed to a delay in exchange for an agreement by Sanyo to draft a new restructuring plan within the three-month period.
Nippon Life has the largest share of the loans at four billion yen.
Sanyo and other insurers could not confirm the agreement on Thursday.

Sanyo has been facing financial difficulties due to problem loans held at affiliated firms and protracted sluggishness in the stock market. To help bail out its group firms, the second-tier brokerage launched a nine-year restructuring programme in the 1994/95 business year.

Sanyo received subordinated loans from several major life insurance companies, including Nippon Life and Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Co Ltd, in an effort to increase its capital and strengthen its financial position.

If the agreement had not been made by the end of Thursday, Sanyo's capital adequacy ratio could have fallen below 120 percent, a level at which the Finance Ministry would have ordered the brokerage to take more drastic restructuring measures to improve its operations, industry sources said.
